The Chernigov-Elets Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Chernigov-Elets Icon of the Theotokos

Elets-Chernigov · Chernigov Spruce Tree

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The Chernigov-Elets icon is linked with the tradition of an appearance in a spruce or fir tree and a monastery near Chernigov. The OCA distinguishes it from another Yelets image with a different observance.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3, 7

What is depicted

The photographed example is a later copy of the named Chernigov-Elets icon. Its inscription commemorates the preservation of Emperor Alexander II and names pupils of the Zlatopol gymnasium with the date 5 February 1880. The old painting and the modern photographer’s CC BY-SA 4.0 grant are separately identified.

[2] Exact artwork file: Description, Creator, Date, Credit and licence fields; complete downloaded image visually compared

History and tradition

The OCA relates an appearance in 1060 and the foundation of a monastery. It follows destruction, concealment, and restoration, but expressly says the original icon’s ultimate fate is unclear. It gives alternative accounts of its movement or disappearance and identifies later copies.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3, 4, 5, 6

The account names Joannicius Golyatovsky and his 1676 collection of miracle narratives in its discussion of the monastery’s restoration and a later copy.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 6

Published explanation

Its February 5 commemoration and Chernigov monastery context identify this particular tradition. The account’s other Yelets icon, commemorated January 11, must not be treated as an interchangeable object merely because the names sound similar. The pictured 1880 example illustrates later reception.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3, 5, 6, 7
